citation: Hayden FG, et al. Ensitrelvir for Covid-19 Postexposure Prophylaxis in Household Contacts. N Engl J Med. 2026. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2509306.
used_for: Arm-specific symptomatic COVID-19 risk; overall all-infection risk; safety; high-risk subgroup efficacy.
limitations: No COVID-19-related hospitalizations or deaths; downstream severe outcomes cannot be estimated directly. Highly immune trial population.

citation: Shionogi & Co., Ltd. Approval of Xocova for prevention of COVID-19 in Japan. Press release, March 23, 2026.
used_for: Approved prevention indication, dose, tablet price, course acquisition cost.
limitations: Manufacturer source; drug price should be rechecked against the official NHI price list at analysis lock.

citation: Center for Outcomes Research and Economic Evaluation for Health. Guideline for Preparing Cost-Effectiveness Evaluation to the Central Social Insurance Medical Council. Approved January 16, 2026.
used_for: Perspective, QALY outcome, Japanese utility preference, costing, discounting, modeling, reproducibility, scenario and probabilistic sensitivity analysis.
limitations: English version is a translation; Japanese version prevails if discrepancies arise.

citation: Yuasa A, Matsuda H, Fujii Y, et al. Cost-effectiveness Analysis of Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir Compared with Molnupiravir in Patients at High Risk for Progression to Severe COVID-19 in Japan. JHEOR. 2025;12(1):75-85. doi:10.36469/001c.129067.
design: Published Japanese hybrid decision-tree and Markov CEA with EHR and claims cost inputs
used_for: Hospitalization and mortality inputs, ICU and ventilation probabilities, acute costs, length of stay, acute utility decrements, oral antiviral administration cost, model precedent.
limitations: Not a PEP study. Some clinical inputs are transferred from other COVID-19 contexts and price year is 2023.

citation: Iba A, Hosozawa M, Hori M, et al. Prevalence of and Risk Factors for Post-COVID-19 Condition during Omicron BA.5-Dominant Wave, Japan. Emerg Infect Dis. 2024;30(7). doi:10.3201/eid3007.231723.
used_for: PCC probability: 11.8% among cases, 5.5% among controls, attributable excess 6.3 percentage points.
limitations: Self-reported symptoms; adults 20 to 69 years; not specific to high-risk or hospitalized patients; duration and treatment cost not estimated.

citation: Tsuzuki S, Miyazato Y, Terada M, Morioka S, Ohmagari N, Beutels P. Impact of long-COVID on health-related quality of life in Japanese COVID-19 patients. Health Qual Life Outcomes. 2022;20:125. doi:10.1186/s12955-022-02033-6.
used_for: PCC utility decrement as transferred in the Japanese CEA.
limitations: Earlier pandemic period; cross-sectional; the 0.027 decrement is a model-derived contrast rather than a direct PEP estimate.

citation: Kamata K, Honda H, Tokuda Y, et al. Post-COVID health-related quality of life and somatic symptoms: a national survey in Japan. Am J Med Sci. 2023;366(2):114-123. doi:10.1016/j.amjms.2023.04.018.
used_for: Baseline and acute COVID-19 utility values transferred through the Japanese CEA.
limitations: Cross-sectional and not designed for PEP; severity mapping from oxygen requirement to model states is approximate.

citation: Uno S, Goto R, Honda K, et al. Healthcare costs for hospitalized COVID-19 patients in a Japanese university hospital: a cross-sectional study. Cost Eff Resour Alloc. 2023;21:43. doi:10.1186/s12962-023-00453-9.
used_for: Hospitalization cost input and source-traceability comparison.
limitations: Single-center 2021 university-hospital cohort; nominal source-year cost was not fully re-priced to 2026; generalizability to current practice is limited.

citation: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare. The 23rd Complete Life Tables, Japan.
used_for: Recommended source for replacing the scalar remaining-QALY-per-death parameter with age-sex specific estimates.
limitations: The repository prototype leaves cohort-specific QALYs lost per death as an editable scalar because target age-sex distribution has not yet been fixed.

citation: Shionogi Inc. New England Journal of Medicine publishes SCORPIO-PEP results. Press release, May 2026.
design: Official manufacturer summary of the peer-reviewed trial
used_for: Cross-check of exact high-risk subgroup counts: 9/382 versus 37/374.
limitations: Manufacturer source; primary publication remains the preferred citation.

citation: Study team structural assumption: PCC computational horizon.
used_for: Base and extended computational horizons for the PCC state-transition module.
limitations: Not empirical evidence. The horizon should be long enough to capture nearly all modeled PCC occupancy.

citation: Study team structural assumption: incremental PEP access and dispensing cost.
used_for: Additional consultation, testing, dispensing, delivery, or implementation cost not captured elsewhere.
limitations: Base value is zero pending micro-costing. Scenario and threshold analyses are required.

citation: Study team cohort-calibration assumption: discounted remaining QALYs lost per acute death.
used_for: Lifetime QALY loss from acute COVID-19 death before the target age-sex distribution is locked.
limitations: Must be replaced by age-sex-specific Japanese life-table survival and utility integration for the final analysis.

citation: Study team structural assumption: PCC risk multiplier after hospitalization.
used_for: Severity-specific PCC incidence after hospitalized versus outpatient symptomatic COVID-19.
limitations: No directly transportable Japanese estimate was identified for the modeled setting.

citation: Study team structural assumption: PCC after asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
used_for: Exploratory any-infection PCC scenario only.
limitations: Excluded from the primary analysis and unsupported by ensitrelvir-specific causal evidence.

citation: Study team structural assumption: mean PCC duration.
design: Internal duration assumption informed by prior economic models
used_for: Mean duration and recovery rate in the monthly PCC state-transition module.
limitations: Japanese longitudinal duration evidence for the target cohort is insufficient; broad DSA and a five-year scenario are included.

citation: Study team evidence-gap assumption: annual direct medical cost of PCC.
used_for: Direct payer cost of post-COVID-19 condition.
limitations: Base value is zero pending matched Japanese claims evidence. Nonzero scenario and threshold analyses are included.

citation: Shiroiwa T, Noto S, Fukuda T. Japanese Population Norms of EQ-5D-5L and Health Utilities Index Mark 3: Disutility Catalog by Disease and Symptom in Community Settings. Value Health. 2021;24(8):1193-1202. doi:10.1016/j.jval.2021.03.010.
design: National population survey with age-sex utility norms
used_for: Recommended source for age-sex-specific background utility in the optional remaining-QALY calibration module.
limitations: Published age bands require transparent mapping to each attained age; use must comply with source and instrument licensing conditions.

citation: Andersen KM, Brouillette MA, Togo K, et al. Inpatient burden of COVID-19 in Japan: a retrospective cohort study. J Infect Chemother. 2025;31:102721. doi:10.1016/j.jiac.2025.102721.
used_for: Contemporary hospitalized-case age, sex, length of stay, ICU use, ventilation, and in-hospital mortality; late-Omicron median age 82 and overall male share 54% inform the death-QALY proxy.
limitations: Hospitalized population is selected and older than the PEP trial. Age and sex of admissions, rather than decedents, are used as a proxy; the study was industry sponsored.

citation: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare. Abridged Life Tables for Japan 2025.
used_for: Age-sex survival probabilities for lifetime QALY loss after acute death.
limitations: Life-table input is truncated at age 105 in the repository; residual survival beyond 105 is omitted.

citation: Maeda H, Igarashi A, Kuwamitsu O, Morimoto K. Comparison of long-term health-related quality of life and symptoms between COVID-19 patients and test-negative controls during the Omicron-predominant period in Japan. Arch Public Health. 2025;83(1):136. doi:10.1186/s13690-025-01625-0.
design: Retrospective online recall survey with a test-negative comparison group
used_for: Acute utility decrement and direct integration of post-acute utility differences from months 1 to 12.
limitations: Single Tokyo clinic; 302 COVID-19 respondents and 77 controls; median age 42; 28.3% response; retrospectively recalled intervals; no prospectively measured baseline utility; recall and response-selection bias; later control utilities were near the ceiling.

citation: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare. FY2026 medical fee schedule and item-level reimbursement database.
used_for: Initial or telemedicine consultation, antigen testing, specimen collection, interpretation, and prescription components for PEP delivery.
limitations: Actual billing depends on setting, simultaneous services, monthly interpretation-fee rules, and patient pathway.

citation: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare. FY2026 dispensing fee schedule.
used_for: Representative community-pharmacy dispensing, preparation, management, and counselling components.
limitations: Pharmacy category, digital prescription use, patient notebook status, and add-on claims may alter reimbursement.

citation: Takazono T, Fujita S, Komeda T, et al. Real-World Effectiveness of Ensitrelvir in Reducing Severe Outcomes in Outpatients at High Risk for COVID-19. Infect Dis Ther. 2024;13(8):1821-1833. doi:10.1007/s40121-024-01010-4.
used_for: Untreated high-risk outpatient 28-day all-cause hospitalization risk and transportability scenarios.
limitations: Few patients were aged 65 years or older, vaccination status was unavailable, hospitalization was all-cause, and exposure was treatment after diagnosis rather than PEP.

citation: Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency. Xocova Tablets 125 mg Japanese package insert, revised August 2026.
used_for: Prevention dose and requirement to start within 72 hours after contact; implementation scenario definition.
limitations: The trial required baseline negativity, while the label does not state that a negative test is mandatory. Local practice may differ.

citation: Study team derived calibration combining Andersen et al. 2025, MHLW 2025 abridged life tables, and Shiroiwa et al. 2021 EQ-5D-5L population norms.
used_for: Discounted remaining QALYs lost per acute COVID-19 death using an age-82, 54%-male proxy cohort.
limitations: Age 82 and 54% male are proxies from hospitalized cases, not decedent-specific distributions. Utilities above age 89 are carried forward from ages 80 to 89 and survival is truncated at age 105.

citation: Study team microcost derived from the FY2026 MHLW medical and pharmacy fee schedules.
used_for: PEP delivery cost for the trial-concordant face-to-face plus antigen-test pathway.
limitations: Excludes travel, productivity, urgent delivery, provider capacity, and unlisted local implementation costs.

citation: Taniguchi T, Hoshino M, Ide R, et al. The continued impact of COVID-19 during the Omicron era on immunocompromised individuals in Japan. J Infect Chemother. 2025;31(12):102840. doi:10.1016/j.jiac.2025.102840.
used_for: Exploratory immunocompromised, B-cell-depleting therapy, and hematologic-malignancy hospitalization-rate multipliers.
limitations: Population incidence-rate ratios are transferred to hospitalization conditional on symptomatic infection. Follow-up was calendar year 2023 and several authors were employed by the sponsor.

citation: Study team structural assumption: acute cost price and practice adjustment factor.
used_for: Sensitivity range around source-year direct acute medical costs.
limitations: A general CPI is not imposed because payer tariffs and case-mix changes are not equivalent to consumer inflation.

citation: Study team structural assumption: direct post-acute medical cost scenarios.
used_for: Scenario values for direct medical spending after surviving symptomatic COVID-19.
limitations: Scenario values are not empirical estimates and must not be described as Japanese observed costs.

citation: Study team structural assumption: acute death only after COVID-19 hospitalization.
used_for: Mortality pathway in the publication base case.
limitations: Out-of-hospital COVID-19 deaths are omitted. This is conservative if such deaths occur and are preventable.

citation: Study team structural assumption: causal attribution of 28-day all-cause hospitalization to symptomatic COVID-19.
used_for: Separates the all-cause hospitalization endpoint used for absolute risk from COVID-19-attributable hospitalization, cost, and mortality in the PEP model.
limitations: No Japanese estimate of the attributable fraction was identified. The base value is 100%, with 50% and 0% structural scenarios; the parameter is not probabilistically sampled.

citation: Study team structural bounding assumption: first-generation downstream symptomatic cases.
used_for: Exploratory 0.2 and 0.5 additional downstream symptomatic cases per directly prevented symptomatic case.
limitations: Not an empirical transmission estimate and not a dynamic transmission model; excludes timing, immunity, clustering, depletion, and further generations.
